content:
maria: Heads up — I hit a reproducible leak in the Go sample app when cancelling generator streaming mid-handshake. App spins up goroutines that never return. :bug:

alex: ugh. can you paste a minimal repro? is this the sampleapp from github.com/redwood-inference/go-sampleapps? :eyes:

maria: yes, the generator-chat sample. repro steps: start a streaming generator, then cancel ctx very early (within ~50-200ms). sometimes the stream closes, sometimes it doesn't and goroutines stick around.

maria: minimal snippet i used:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 200*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, params)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
// read first token or cancel
for {
  tok, err := stream.Recv()
  if err != nil { break }
  fmt.Print(tok.Text)
}
```

maria: when ctx times out while the SDK is still in the handshake, some internal goroutines wait on token refresh or a channel and never exit. i see auth-refresh goroutine + stream write goroutine stacking up.

jon: that sounds like the auth refresh race we discussed 2 weeks ago. handshake path doesn't attach ctx Done to the refresh loop. if token refresh blocks (network hiccup) it won't wake the stream cancel.

alex: ok, this is probably two issues: (1) the generator stream handshake should be cancellable (respect ctx) and (2) the sample app should call stream.Close() or provide an explicit Cancel() on the stream to guarantee cleanup. we never exposed Close() on the stream in the old API because we expected ctx-based cancellations to suffice. clearly not reliable.

sam: agree with alex. DX-wise, users expect cancel to stop everything. leaking goroutines is a showstopper for onboarding. quick fix idea: document the pattern and add a Close() method on Stream that cancels internal goroutine(s). longer fix: plumb ctx into auth refresh and transport handshake.

maria: workaround that worked for me: wrap client.Transport with a custom RoundTripper that respects ctx and short-circuits token refresh, then call stream.Cancel() in the example (i added stream.Cancel = func() { cancel() } hack). not ideal to teach hacks though.

alex: can you share the heap/profile? want to see stack traces. also: which Go SDK version?

maria: sdk v0.9.1. i'll attach pprof in the sampleapp repo. profile shows goroutines stuck in tokenProvider.refresh -> time.Sleep / net.Dial.

ci-bot: build/test: generator-sampleapp (pr/482) — flaky ✓  (ran in 2m14s)

jon: proposed immediate patch: in generator.Stream() before starting any goroutine, start a watcher goroutine that selects on ctx.Done() and a done chan. when ctx.Done() fires, close internal channels and call transport.CancelRequest. also add Stream.Close() that triggers same flow. backward compatible if Close() is no-op when stream finished.

alex: i'll take the SDK change. plan: add Close() and plumb ctx into token refresh call site. can we also add a short doc blurb in sampleapp with an explicit cancellation example and call out auth-refresh caveat?

maria: thanks — adding that doc snippet would have saved me ~2 hours. happy to PR sampleapp doc once patch lands.

sam: small follow-ups: (a) add an e2e test that cancels during handshake (b) add lint rule comment in sampleapp pointing at Close() pattern (c) consider adding telemetry to detect abandoned streams (gc probe)

alex: noted. i'll open draft PR (#1367) for the SDK and link it here once ready. expected ETA: tomorrow morning.

maria: ping me on the PR — i can attach my repro and heap. thanks! :pray:

ci-bot: deploy: staging — generator-service v1.8.2 rolled out to 3/3 hosts

jon: one more thing — we should validate that dedicated/private runtimes don't surface different timing (network latency can make this easier to hit). adding test matrix to the e2e.

alex: added task to the PR checklist. thanks everyone.
